title: Near or far: where do 1/d links land?
hook: Nearer distances are likelier. How much likelier is a near band than a far one?

doesNotKnow: why: with chance ∝ 1/d, a link is equally likely to land 1–2, 2–4, … or 256–512 away

misconception: With 1/d links most links are very short.
objective: The learner can explain that with chance ∝ 1/d each doubling band of distances holds twice as many distances, each half as likely, so every band gets about the same share of links (2–3 away: 12.2%; 256–512 away: 10.2% on a ring of 1,024).

claims.text: With chance ∝ 1/d on a ring of 1,024, band 2–3 gets 12.2% of links and band 256–512 gets 10.2% (reveal: 'band 2–3 got 12.2% and 256–512 got 10.2%').
claims.source: Demo.tsx shares(): exact sums over d = 1..512 with 2 people at each d < 512 and 1 at d = 512, weight (people at d)/d, bands 1, 2–3, 4–7, …, 128–255, 256–512. Builder's Node run 2026-10-14: 14.7, 12.2, 11.1, 10.6, 10.4, 10.3, 10.2, 10.2, 10.2 (%). Matches the brief's check. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Own node sums (fc21b/ring.mjs), people(d) = 2 for d < 512, 1 at 512: q=1 bands 14.7 12.2 11.1 10.6 10.4 10.3 10.2 10.2 10.2 (%). | v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave H r8 phone fit): reveal wording shortened ('of links' dropped); reopened, unverified. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node sums (people 2 per distance, 1 at 512): q=1 bands 14.7 12.2 11.1 10.6 10.4 10.3 10.2 10.2 10.2 %. Reveal prints pct(SHARES[R1][1]) and [8]: 12.2% and 10.2%.

claims.text: With 1/d links, every band from 2–3 out gets 10–12% of links.
claims.source: Same sums as c1: bands 2 to 9 range from 12.2% down to 10.2%; the band of distance 1 alone gets 14.7%. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Same sums: bands 2-3 to 256-512 run 12.2% to 10.2%, i.e. 10-12% to whole percent (12.2 rounds to 12). Builder may prefer 'about 10-12%' since the stage shows 12.2%.

claims.text: Each band holds twice as many distances as the one before, and with 1/d each of those distances is half as likely, so the two cancel (reveal: 'each half as likely, so the two cancel').
claims.source: Band [2^k, 2^(k+1)) has 2^k distances, each with weight between 2^-(k+1) and 2^-k, so its total weight is between 1/2 and 1 for every k (it tends to ln 2 ≈ 0.69 of a unit). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Re-derived: band [2^k, 2^(k+1)) has 2^k distances, each weight in (2^-(k+1), 2^-k], total in (1/2, 1], tending to ln 2. Last band 256-512 holds 257 distances (one person at 512), approximately double. | v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave H r8 phone fit): reveal wording shortened; reopened, unverified. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Re-derived: band [2^k, 2^(k+1)) has 2^k distances, each with 1/d weight in (2^-(k+1), 2^-k], total in (1/2, 1], tending to ln 2; last band 256-512 has 257 distances. 'Each half as likely' read as 'each distance about half as likely as one in the band before': true.

claims.text: Uniform links put 50.1% of links in the farthest band (256–512); 1/d² links put 60.9% at distance 1. Shown on the stage only, as the dashed outlines' labels 'Uniform 50.1%' and '1/d² 60.9%'; the reveal sentence was cut in v4 for the phone-fit word budget.
claims.source: Demo.tsx shares() with q = 0 and q = 2: uniform 513 of 1,023 people are 256–512 away = 50.1%; 1/d² band 1 = 2/(sum of people(d)/d²) = 60.9% (builder's Node run, 2026-10-14). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Own sums: q=0 last band 513/1023 people = 50.15% -> 50.1%; q=2 band 1 = 60.9%. | v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave H r8 phone fit): reveal sentence cut, the stage labels carry the fact; reopened, unverified. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own sums: q=0 band 256-512 = 513/1023 people = 50.1%; q=2 band 1 = 60.9%. Ghosts: a seen rule other than the current one and 1/d leaves a dashed outline of its tallest bar with label 'Uniform 50.1%' (band 256-512) / '1/d² 60.9%' (band 1). Milestones q0 and q2 are required, so under 1/d both labels are on stage.

claims.text: Wherever a message is, a link that halves its remaining distance is about equally likely: that is why 1/d links route fast.
claims.source: Easley and Kleinberg (2010) ch. 20 (advanced material on decentralised search); Kleinberg (2000), Nature 406 and STOC 2000. From the brief; builder has not opened these. Attribution: fact-checker confirms. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Own check on this ring: probability one 1/d link lands within D/2 of the target from distance D is 10.6, 8.7, 8.2, 8.1, 10.2% for D = 4, 16, 64, 256, 512 (uniform: 0.5% to 50%; 1/d^2: 15% to 0.1%), so roughly constant only for 1/d. Own greedy-routing simulation (400 trials): mean steps q=0 28.5, q=1 24.0, q=2 116.9, so 1/d does route fast here; note q=0.5 gave 21.7, so at n = 1,024 1/d is fast but not measurably the fastest, and the lesson must not say it is. Kleinberg (2000, Nature 406; STOC 2000) and E&K ch. 20 (advanced section on decentralized search) cited from memory, not opened (hosts blocked); the sentence is verified on the derivation and simulation. | v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave H r8 phone fit): now the second sentence of reveal paragraph 2; reopened, unverified. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Rests on own derivation and simulation; Kleinberg 2000 and Easley-Kleinberg ch. 20 not opened (web blocked). Own exact sums: chance one link from distance D lands within D/2 of the target = 10.6, 8.7, 8.2, 8.1, 10.2% (D = 4, 16, 64, 256, 512) under 1/d, against 0.5-50% uniform and 15-0.1% under 1/d². Own greedy routing (one long link per node, 400 trials): q=0 27.1, q=0.5 23.7, q=1 22.8, q=2 122.1 steps. So 1/d routes fast here; the sentence does not say fastest, and it should not (q=0.5 is close at n = 1,024).

claims.text: Band 2–3 holds two distances against 257 in band 256–512, yet with 1/d links the two get about equal shares.
claims.source: Unrecorded reveal sentence found by fact-checker pass 21 (2026-10-14), reveal paragraph 1: "two distances against 257, about equal". Recorded, not verified by the recorder; needs an independent check (bands from Demo BANDS: 2–3 and 256–512; shares from c1). · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: Own sums, ring of 1,024 with 1/d: band 2-3 gets 12.2%, band 256-512 gets 10.2%; distances 2 vs 512 - 256 + 1 = 257. 'About equal' against a 128-fold difference in distances is fair. The sentence is the builder's; a pass-21 fact-checker session recorded it, and this is a separate session.

The Band slider's value uses the same form for the chosen band (e.g. '8–15: 8 × 1/8 to 1/15 → 10.6%'). The reveal no longer restates 0.42 and 0.0027.

claims.text: With 1/d links on a ring of 1,024, about 1.2 times as many links land 2–3 away as 256–512 away (12.2% against 10.2%), though each 2–3 distance is far likelier than each 256–512 distance.
claims.source: Demo.tsx RATIO = 12.2 / 10.2 at the stage's one-decimal rounding = 1.196 -> '1.2'. Unrounded shares from shares(1): 0.1222 / 0.1018 ≈ 1.20. Per-distance chance: 0.42 vs 0.0027 (c7), about 150 times. Answer key: the question asks 'how many times as many links land 2–3 away as 256–512 away'; options About 100× / About 10× / About 1×, answer About 1×. Builder revision v3 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave G r7). Builder statement, not self-verified. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Unrounded shares 0.1222 / 0.1018 = 1.199; RATIO from the one-decimal shares 12.2/10.2 = 1.196 -> '1.2'. Per-distance chance 0.4167 vs 0.00271, about 154 times. Answer key 'About 1×' (index 2) is the nearest option to 1.2. | v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave H r8 phone fit): reveal wording changed around it; reopened, unverified. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. recall.question: Long links land at distance d with chance ∝ 1/d. Which is more likely: a link 4–7 away, or one 128–255 away?
recall.why: The far band holds 32 times as many distances, but each is about 32 times less likely, so the two bands get about the same share (11.1% vs 10.2% on a ring of 1,024).
